discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body systems with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Zoller and co-workers proposed in 1998 that ultracold atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model with tunable parameters, turning Feynman's idea of a quantum simulator into a concrete programme. Greiner and Bloch observed the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator quantum phase transition in 2002, opening the field of strongly correlated quantum gases. They then developed quantum gas microscopes that image and control individual atoms in lattices, revealing antiferromagnetic correlations in the Fermi-Hubbard model, string order, many-body localization, entanglement entropy and thermalization in isolated quantum systems. This work created a new field in which basic questions of many-body physics, such as quantum phase transitions, non-equilibrium dynamics and quantum thermalization, can be studied with precise experimental control. It now underpins atom-based quantum simulation and computation worldwide.
